title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is computing the 'fundamental group with operators' of the Teichmüller groupoid in modular dimension 0, S_0T_{0,I}. Its object set is ω(I), the two-element torsor of orientations (cyclic orders) of I, on which S_I acts through the sign. The groupoid is obtained from a connected Z-groupoid on ω(I) by changing the operator group along the diagonal Z → Z^I; the Z^I are the boundary (Dehn) twists. The previous page defines π_1(S_0T_{0,I}, S_I; x) as pairs (α, l), with α in S_I and l a path from x to αx, composed by (l,α)(l',α') = (l + α(l'), αα'). This gives an extension G(I) of S_I by Z^I.

This page identifies that extension.

Construction:
1. Start from the extension (14): 0 → Z --2--> Z → Z/2 ≅ μ_2 → 0.
2. Pull it back along sgn: S_I → μ_2. This gives E = {(m, α) ∈ Z × S_I : m ≡ sgn(α) mod 2}, an extension of S_I by Z.
3. Push E out along diag: Z → Z^I. The result is G(I).

Non-splitting: restrict to a transposition subgroup ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/2 with σ = (i j). Then push out along a coordinate projection pr_k: Z^I → Z. Since pr_k ∘ diag = id, you recover the extension (14), 0 → Z → Z → Z/2 → 0. That extension is non-split because Z is torsion-free: a lift (σ, 1) squares to the generator 2 ∈ Z. Hence G(I) is non-split.

Splitting over the even part: over S_I^+ (the alternating group, which is the stabiliser of x in S_I) the sign is trivial. So the pullback is canonically split by α ↦ (0, α), formula (19), consistent with (17)-(18). In particular the square of a lift of a transposition is the diagonal element (1,…,1) of Z^I.

Purpose: the next page shows G(I) is independent of x. It carries an outer S_I-action without a global splitting. G(I) is then used to describe S_0T_G for MD groups of modular dimension 0 as products over the vertices s of pieces S_0T_{0,Â_s}. This is a building block (the 'pair of pants' level) of Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower / Lego game.
errors: No mathematical error. The non-splitting argument (project to one coordinate, restrict to a transposition, recover 0→Z→Z→Z/2→0) and the canonical splitting over S_I^+ are both correct.

Minor point: the sign convention (lift of a transposition squares to +diag(1,…,1)) depends on how boundary orientations are chosen (all boundaries 'outgoing'). With mixed in/out conventions one would instead get the familiar balancing-type relation c^2 = θ_{12}·θ_1^{-1}·θ_2^{-1}. This is a convention, not an error.

ideas.what: π_1 of the dimension-0 Teichmüller groupoid with S_I-operators is the extension of S_I by Z^I obtained from 0→Z→Z→Z/2→0 by pulling back along sgn and pushing out along diag
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of a 3-holed sphere with framed boundaries, boundaries allowed to be permuted (extension of S_3 by Z^3 by boundary twists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in mapping class group theory; appears implicitly in the Lego-Teichmüller / Moore–Seiberg literature (Moore–Seiberg 1989; Bakalov–Kirillov; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the Lego game in modular dimension ≤1, but not this explicit extension computation

ideas.what: Non-splitting via restriction to a transposition subgroup and projection to one factor; canonical splitting over the alternating group (stabiliser of an orientation)
ideas.modern_name: Elementary group extension computation (pullback/pushout of extensions, torsion obstruction)

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but routine computation of an extension of S_I by Z^I (a framed pair-of-pants mapping class group with permutations), done as part of Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower notes. The content is standard and reflected in the later Lego/Moore–Seiberg literature; nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Above 'image inverse' the marginal insertion is 'μ_2', i.e. the inverse image via sgn: S_I → μ_2.
'σ_K' is likely 'σ_k' (lowercase), denoting the order-2 subgroup generated by the transposition (i,j).

Garbled passage likely reads roughly: 'car en envoyant[?] par la projection Z^I → Z correspondant à [un indice] ... on trouve une extension de σ_k par Z qui n'est autre ... que l'extension (14)'. 'Cpx' is probably a misreading.
'et ... les stabilisateurs de x dans S_I' should read approximately 'qui est le stabilisateur de x dans S_I, est évidemment canoniquement scindée'.
The final line labels formulas (17), (18) in the left margin and then (19): α ↦ (0, α), α ∈ S_I^+.
